why: The new example hands over practice.2's answer: 'Hola, ¿cómo te llamas?' (unchanged) is now this example's second sentence with Hola added, i.e. a shortened copy.
fix: Mucho gusto. Me llamo Diego. (en: Nice to meet you. My name's Diego.) ¿cómo te llamas? stays taught by the notice and practice.0's ask.

text: Tienes muchas bolsas y no puedes abrir la puerta. ¿Qué pides?
why: The question contains its answer: 'puedes abrir la puerta' gives the learner the verb, the object and almost the form of '¿Me puede abrir la puerta?'.
fix: Tienes las manos llenas de bolsas y la puerta está cerrada. ¿Qué pides? (en: Your hands are full of bags and the door is closed. What do you ask?)

text: En la farmacia hay un señor. Es la tarde. ¿Qué dices?
why: The lesson teaches choosing the title; saying 'un señor' in the question gives away the title in the answer 'Buenas tardes, señor' (the other two asks use chico and vecina mayor instead).
fix: En la farmacia hay un hombre. Es de tarde. ¿Qué dices? (en: There's a man at the pharmacy. It's afternoon. What do you say?)

why: Broke the unchanged notice: with limones replaced by mangos (here and in practice.2), no example or answer shows the -es plural the notice teaches ('-es after a consonant: tacos, limones'); every plural is now -s.
fix: Aquí tiene: dos melones. (en: Here you go: two melons.)

text: Limón in Mexico is the small green lime.
why: Broke the unchanged context: limón no longer appears anywhere in the lesson, so this note explains nothing the learner hears.
fix: (empty) — or, if the notice keeps 'limones' as its -es example, leave the notice and drop only this context line.
